name: Meat
lede: Meat is a warm salmon-orange, the English rendering of *Shishi-iro*, a traditional Japanese color name that reads literally as "meat-color."

sections.title: A color named for flesh
sections.body:
Our library files this hue from the Japanese traditional-colors list under *Shishi-iro* (猪色), given in our data as meaning "meat-color" [1]. Japanese traditional names routinely describe a hue by the material it resembles rather than a mixed-pigment recipe, the way English has *salmon* and *flesh* [1].

Nearest named neighbors by measured color are [[conch-shell]] and [[dark-salmon]], both close duller cousins, with [[light-salmon]] and [[dusty-coral]] a little further off [1]. The screen swatch is a modern approximation; no physical dye sample backs it [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 23 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.1 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 14 [2]. That makes it rarer than 65 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in paintings from the 1800s, at 1.0 times the expected rate for that century [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 64 percent of the 14 paintings where it appears, ranked by lightness so varnish cannot fake the result [2]. The earliest dated painting with it is from 1333, a work attributed to Bernardo Daddi, though the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first [2].
